metadata.description: Omnium: a local marketplace of Claude Code plugins, shipped as committed zero-dependency source. The plugin roster is the `plugins` array below.

plugins.name: cautium
plugins.description: An always-on, zero-config security conscience: a single SessionStart hook injects a three-layer primer into every session — universal security duties (secrets, injection-safe input, least-privilege authN/Z, supply-chain and crypto hygiene), a universal 0-10 change-impact rubric, and an OS-dependent risk mapping keyed on process.platform. No commands, no state, cross-platform.

plugins.name: contextum
plugins.description: Context management around a task: /contextum:prepare <topic> gathers the code, tests, history, and recorded decisions a coming task will need into the conversation (the main agent reads them itself), then reports a short, checkable briefing — the interpretation it chose, anchors marked read vs. inferred, and what it did not find or examine — so a miss is visible before the task starts; /contextum:report [task] audits the current context against that task or the whole session — dead weight with its source (environment injections, the agent's own loads, user attachments) and weak spots where the agent relies on assumptions rather than examined material, each with the step that would firm it up. Fully standalone: two markdown commands; no hooks, no MCP server, no state.

plugins.name: distillum
plugins.description: A session-knowledge distiller: /distillum:to-skill turns a procedure the session figured out into a reusable skill (user- or project-level, with dedup, placement, and replay-test quality gates); /distillum:to-docs folds declarative knowledge (decisions, constraints, how things actually work) into the project's existing documentation home, fixing drift when found. Fully standalone: two markdown commands; no hooks, no MCP server, no state.

plugins.name: expertum
plugins.description: Provides /expertum:review, /expertum:research, /expertum:interview, /expertum:conduct, and /expertum:conduct-mvp. Review and research fan the task out to read-only analysts — one expertum:analyst sub-agent taking on any of 54 expert lenses served as data (expertum_overview / expertum_expert), so the agent roster carries one line, not 54 — that emit one Markdown report each into a per-run .expertum/<timestamp>--<name>/ folder via a bundled zero-dependency MCP server; interview walks the user through questionnaires to turn a vague idea into a pinned brief; conduct adds an autonomous plan->implement->expert-review loop; conduct-mvp is the same loop scoped to a minimal build.

plugins.name: graphyne
plugins.description: TDD gate (failing-test required before editing gated source) + a bidirectional related-files graph (MCP) with adoption hooks, per git project.

plugins.name: memosyne
plugins.description: Session-independent task memory (MCP) + adoption hooks for git projects.

plugins.name: sessio
plugins.description: An always-on, cross-platform SessionStart hook that routes temporary/generated files into a per-task dated subdirectory (<base>/YYYY-MM-DD--<desc>) of a scratch root read from the CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR environment variable; when the var is unset it onboards the user to set it. No commands, no state.

plugins.name: statusline
plugins.description: Ships a custom, cross-platform Claude Code status line. Since a plugin cannot declare a statusLine itself, a single SessionStart hook copies the self-contained renderer into the persistent per-plugin data dir (stable across version bumps) and nudges the agent to install a one-line statusLine command pointing at it — asking first if a foreign statusLine already exists. The renderer is pure Node built-ins, renders from the status payload on stdin, and fails open. No commands, no state.
